newsitem.title: IRAQ: UAE men deliver humanitarian supplies to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: UAE men deliver humanitarian supplies to Iraq.

text.p: A group of men from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) arrived in Baghdad on Monday with 32 tonnes of baby milk and medicine for the sanctions-hit Iraqi people.
They visited Saddam hospital and were seen caressing malnourished Iraqi babies and holding them in their arms.

"Our visit is in harmony with the initiative of UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan on the necessity of putting an end to differences in the Arab arena," Isa Murad Hassan, one of the group members, told reporters.

The UAE president is the most vociferous among Gulf Arab leaders in calling for reconciliation with Baghdad and the lifting of sanctions on Iraq slapped for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Kuwait and Saudi Arabia are the most adamant in favour of keeping the sanctions in place.
Sheikh Zaid's peaceful overtures have led to an increased volume of trade between the two countries. Iraqi traders say they now find duty-free Dubai easier to deal with than neighbouring countries.
"We feel that this visit is the first step towards lifting the embargo on Iraq. We believe the sanctions are unfair," Hassan told reporters.

The group said they had slaughtered sheep as soon as they reached Iraqi soil following their 50-hour voyage across the Gulf as a sign of their jubilation for the safety of President Saddam Hussein's eldest son who was shot and wounded in Baghdad on December 12.
They told hospital authorities they were ready to meet their needs and would try to send them more supplies.
Another member, Khalifa Muttar al-Aqroubi, described sanctions on Iraq as vicious and said: "We the people of the UAE denounce the continuation of this damned embargo and will work to break it."
He said the group had an office in Dubai to collect donations for Iraq. "Shortly we will launch a campaign in support of Iraq in which Dubai and UAE televisions will take part," he said.
Raad Badawi al-Ali said the visit was approved by the UAE authorities and had the blessing of Defence Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Rashid al-Maktoum who is also crown prince of the emirate of Dubai.
Ali said the supplies they brought to the Iraqi people were worth 1.5 million dirhams ($410,000).
